call.text: Revenue +36% to ₹6,124 cr, EBITDA (incl. other income) +21% to ₹742 cr, PAT ₹393 cr (incl. ₹21.8 cr exceptional gain). Volume +4% to 9.85 lakh t: DAP +55% (policy makes DAP more profitable than NPK), NPK −9%, urea −16%.

EBITDA ~₹7,000/t vs ~₹6,500/t a year earlier, 'mainly on account of the stock' bought before prices rose, plus full running of the new sulphuric acid plants. Management called ~₹5,000/t realistic for the year.

70-75% of global sulphur and ammonia trade passes through the Strait of Hormuz; sulphur bought spot ($1,000+ at end-July); ammonia diversified to South-East Asia; OCP supplies rock and acid without issues.

DAP sells at ₹1,350 a bag vs ₹2,100-2,500 for NPKs; NPK prices raised ₹400-500 a bag; industry expects the government to cover part of the cost increase; the farmer shift back to NPK needs the gap to fall to ~₹200 a bag.

Subsidy outstanding ₹4,600 cr at 30-Jun-2026 (₹3,800 cr at the May call; ₹3,780 cr at Dec-2025); ₹2,650 cr received in Q1; gross debt ₹6,500 cr (₹6,872 cr at Mar-2026). FY26 operating cash flow was −₹1,012 cr on a deliberate ~30-day extra raw-material stock.
Phosphatic market ~24 mt (DAP ~10 mt, NPK ~14 mt; NPK 20:20:0:13 6-7 mt); farmer-level industry growth ~1% in Q1 vs PPL +15-16%.

corporateActions: IPO in May-2022 (₹975 cr of fresh share proceeds in the FY23 cash flow); 22.16 cr shares issued to MCFL shareholders on 3-Dec-2025 (equity ₹815 cr → ₹1,038 cr); ESOP allotments otherwise. No bonus, split or buyback found. Dividends: ₹1.00 for FY25 (paid FY26), ₹1.50 proposed for FY26.

governance.auditor: B S R & Co. LLP; emphasis of matter on restating FY25 from the NCLT appointed date (overriding Ind AS 103, which would have accounted from 16-Oct-2025); key audit matters: subsidy revenue, MCFL purchase-price allocation
governance.relatedParty: OCP group entities supplied ~₹8,200 cr in FY26 (IMACID phosphoric acid ₹2,541 cr, Phosboucraa rock ₹2,087 cr, OCP Nutricrops TSP ₹1,416 cr, OCP SA rock and acid ₹809 cr, Kofert/Jorf DAP and TSP ₹1,373 cr), about half of raw-material and traded purchases; Zuari FarmHub bought ₹309 cr of fertilisers; Simon India (group) supplied ₹57 cr of plant
governance.pledge: Jun-2026: 9.21 cr promoter shares pledged (15.3% of promoter holding, 8.9% of the company): ZMPPL 6.50 cr, ZACL 2.71 cr (41% of ZACL's stake). ZMPPL reported release of ~6.49 cr pledged shares on 19-Aug-2026 (secondary source)

accounting.text: ₹11,625 cr of FY26 revenue (53%) is government subsidy (₹2,088 cr on traded goods), recognised at notified rates on sale; receivable ₹3,847 cr at Mar-2026 and ₹4,600 cr at Jun-2026. Key audit matter.

FY25 restated from the NCLT appointed date (1-Apr-2024) under acquisition accounting with a provisional purchase-price allocation (goodwill ₹139 cr); the auditor flags that Ind AS 103 alone would have started consolidation on 16-Oct-2025. FY24 and earlier are PPL alone.
₹145 cr of exchange loss on foreign-currency borrowings (buyer's credit for imports) sits in finance cost in FY26 (₹46 cr in FY25), plus ₹50 cr of other exchange loss in other expenses.

FY26: −₹39 cr Labour Code charge (exceptional); Q1FY27: +₹21.8 cr reversal; FY26 loss on discard of plant ₹56 cr (Screener nets it in other income); FY26 'other income' includes ₹59 cr of mutual-fund gains.

About half of purchases come from OCP group companies at contract prices; this secures supply (no rock or acid shortage in the crisis) but means margins depend partly on prices agreed with a shareholder.
